title: Prove an integral quaternion channel gap
body:
## Summary

This scoped proof gives a $2\times2$ response with rational quaternion rank **one**, Lipschitz-order inner rank **two**, and dyadic inner rank **one**. The response is `[[1+i, i+k], [1+j, i+j]]`. In an integral one-channel factorization the first row of the right factor would have entries $d,dh$ with $h=(1+i+j+k)/2$. Integrality of $dh$ forces an even norm for $d$. The norm-two first-column entries have no common norm-two right divisor. The displayed dyadic outer product attains one channel using a single exact halving of a four-lane sum.

The coefficient obstruction and matching construction were produced by Nick Petalas. Dugongue framed the integral and dyadic question in RQ10 and supplied the query-to-factorization implication. Machiavelo and Roçadas supply the classical nonassociate norm-two example. [Atlas PR #5803](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5803) · [Lipschitz integer arithmetic](https://www.cmup.pt/sites/default/files/2024-09/1201.5817v2.pdf) · [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19718458)

## Evidence

The written argument proves the channel counts. The exact checker verifies both lane formulas on eight rational basis inputs, covers all 16 parity classes, and tests all 24 possible norm-two integral divisors. Eight divide each first-column entry individually and zero divide both. Reversing the order of $ij$ changes four basis responses.

Both registered commands passed locally on CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64, with the standard library. Each took 0.01 seconds. The five committed files passed byte, mode and source-history checks. The committed package export passed its integrity check.

Run from the repository root.

```sh
python3.12 -I -W error -B research/lipschitz-channel-gap/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/lipschitz-channel-gap/verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/lipschitz-channel-gap
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/lipschitz-channel-gap --check-source-history
```

Expected marker `PASS_LIPSCHITZ_CHANNEL_GAP basis=8 parity=16 norm_two=24 individual=8,8 common=0 reversed_order_failures=4`.

## Scope and limitations

The proof concerns one formal response over the specified quaternion coefficients. A live caller, physical query realization, exact halving on the reached grid, dirty restoration and the complete bill remain open. The result establishes no new multiplication exponent saving. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. The selected cold replay, predecessor scientific replays, Lean and Docker were outside this package's verification scope.

## Open next questions

- Determine whether dyadic localization preserves rational quaternion rank for every rectangular response. Start with column reduction over the Hurwitz order and track the denominators of the factor entries.
- Find a reached caller boundary supporting the signed-permutation dictionary and a commuting query. Price the dyadic half, source preservation and scratch restoration on the actual input grid.

## Related open work

The inspected open PRs and claims yielded no other study of this quaternion response or its coefficient-order channel gap.
